observation: blank/whitespace-only lines are skipped via Python str.strip() truthiness
resolution: original resolution used JS trim and was incomplete; superseded after publication by exact Python whitespace rule R-008 and G-012

observation: argparse applies Python int() to the token; int() allows surrounding whitespace, leading +/-, digit-group underscores, base-10 only; rejects floats/hex
decision_needed: how port parses the remove number
resolution: implement pyInt() mirroring CPython int(str) base-10 (trim, optional sign, underscores between digits, reject empty/float/hex); on failure raise the argparse invalid-int error

observation: remove -1 → number=-1 (exit 1), i.e. -1 is a positional value, not an option; argparse does this because no option strings look like negative numbers
decision_needed: how port distinguishes options from negative-number values
resolution: replicate argparse: when a token matches a negative-number pattern and no defined option looks like a negative number, treat it as a positional value
evidence: R-014; evidence remove -1 → "error: no note number -1" exit 1 (source capture)

observation: source resolves the path once at module import; a port could resolve per-invocation
decision_needed: when to resolve the store path
resolution: resolve per-invocation (read env NOTES_FILE else $HOME/.notes.txt); observationally identical for a single CLI process (each invocation is one process)

observation: suggestions are formatted with Python repr(); command names are simple ASCII lowercase so repr(x) == "'"+x+"'"
decision_needed: how port renders the quoted names
resolution: implement pyRepr for these ASCII strings (single quotes); command set is fixed {add,list,search,remove} so single-quote form is exact

observation: success/help return 0; remove-out-of-range returns 1; all argparse parse errors exit 2 (argparse raises SystemExit(2)); no subcommand → print_help, return 0
resolution: main(argv:string[]):number returns the code; parse errors throw ParserExit(code=2) caught by main; entry does process.exit(main(argv))

observation: search prints each note's ORIGINAL 1-based index, not a match counter
resolution: iterate all notes with index i (1-based); print "i. note" only when term matches; do not renumber matches

observation: missing-required and invalid-int errors print the SUBparser usage/prog; invalid-choice and unrecognized-arguments print the TOP-level usage/prog (even after a subparser ran)
decision_needed: which parser owns each error message
resolution: implement per R-003: subparser owns type/required errors; top-level owns invalid-choice and the final unrecognized-arguments sweep
evidence: R-003; source captures c6/c11 (sub) vs c9-c12 (top)

observation: a lone/surplus "--" is reported literally as "unrecognized arguments" (e.g. `notes --` exit 2; `notes list --` exit 2; `notes list -- extra` → "-- extra"), while a "--" a positional can consume is removed (`notes -- add hello`, `notes add -- hello`, `notes add -- --` → text "--")
decision_needed: how the port routes the "--" separator
resolution: top: first "--" toggles positional-only, consumed if a subcommand follows else pushed as unrecognized "--"; subparser: "--" consumed when the parser has a positional, else pushed literally to extras in order
evidence: R-003+RA-001; source probes in port/judge/results/phase2-stress.txt (14 "--" cases, 70/70 match)

source_site: cli.py remove type=int (CPython int() Unicode support)
observation: Python int() also parses Unicode Nd digits; port's ASCII-only regex rejects them
decision_needed: whether to reproduce Unicode int parsing
resolution: accept bounded divergence D-002 (ASCII-only); reproducing Unicode Nd parsing is disproportionate and out of exercised surface
evidence: D-002; adversarial probe `remove ٣` src exit1 "no note number 3" vs port exit2 invalid-int (port/judge/results/phase3-adversarial.txt)

observation: ECMAScript trim removes U+FEFF that Python retains and does not remove U+001C that Python treats as whitespace
decision_needed: whether to approve a divergence or implement exact strip truthiness
resolution: implement the explicit CPython whitespace set for whitespace-only detection; retain accepted line contents unchanged; exact parity is practical

observation: URL string equality fails when argv uses /tmp while import.meta.url resolves /private/tmp, so direct invocation can produce no output
decision_needed: how to recognize the same entry file through symlinked path components
resolution: compare filesystem realpaths of process.argv[1] and fileURLToPath(import.meta.url); verify logical, physical, and explicit symlink paths
evidence: PC-001; verify.sh entry probes; verify pass-3 receipt
